## 1. Load and Inspect the Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

nhanes <- read_csv(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

raw_row_count <- nrow(nhanes)
raw_column_count <- ncol(nhanes)

raw_row_count
raw_column_count
```

## 2. Define a Reusable Summary Function

```{r}
summarise_bmi <- function(data) {
  data |>
    filter(
      !is.na(BMI),
      !is.na(IncomeGroup),
      !is.na(Gender)
    ) |>
    group_by(IncomeGroup, Gender) |>
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
      median_bmi = median(BMI),
      sd_bmi = sd(BMI),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(IncomeGroup, Gender)
}
```

## 3. Calculate the Summary

```{r}
nhanes_filtered <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(IncomeGroup),
    !is.na(Gender)
  )

bmi_summary <- summarise_bmi(nhanes)

filtered_row_count <- nrow(nhanes_filtered)
number_of_groups <- nrow(bmi_summary)

filtered_row_count
number_of_groups

bmi_summary
```

## 4. Rounded Summary Values

```{r}
bmi_summary |>
  mutate(
    mean_bmi = round(mean_bmi, 2),
    median_bmi = round(median_bmi, 2),
    sd_bmi = round(sd_bmi, 2)
  )
```

## 5. R Exercise 1: BMI by Gender

This exercise calculates the mean BMI for each gender after removing missing BMI values.

```{r}
nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(Gender)) |>
  group_by(Gender) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## 6. R Exercise 2: BMI by Income Group

This exercise calculates the mean and median BMI for each income group after removing missing values.

```{r}
nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup)) |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 2),
    median_bmi = round(median(BMI), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(IncomeGroup)
```
